newsitem.title: USA: Phelps Dodge settles tribal water dispute.
newsitem.headline: Phelps Dodge settles tribal water dispute.

text.p: Phelps Dodge Corp agreed to pay the San Carlos Apache tribe $25,000 per month for the use of its reservation lands to settle a long-running water rights dispute, the U.S. Interior Department said Wednesday.

The tribe and the U.S. mining company have battled for the last six years over water that Phelps Dodge has been diverting from the Black River and from groundwater next to the reservation to its copper mine in Morenci, Arizona.
Under the agreement, the San Carlos Apache will lease about 14,000 acre feet of water to the company for $5 million up front and about $1 million per year.
Phelps Dodge will also pay all costs to operate, maintain and replace the pump station and pipeline facilities used by the mine, said the Interior Department, which negotiated the settlement.
The Tribe agreed to dismiss a damage claim brought in Tribal Court against the company, but reserved the right to go to federal court for past damages.
Terms of the agreement will be added to emergency funding legislation that lawmakers are working to complete this week.
Phelps Dodge officials were not immediately available to comment on the agreement.
